# Versions of Google Earth (desktop, web, mobile)
981K Views635 Upvotes
_Updated 15 August 2025_
There are three different versions of Google Earth: desktop, web and mobile. This guide attempts to give an overview of the different options available in each.
**Google Earth Pro for desktop**
![](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXc7rETl7WprFgRphJ7aQwK7d3rbFRsQobCX0aDevFwD_S4L85TOFanznuek9NTPK_uMLPgzz4eWxQ3pNXN-Odn-mP_NQlN-HF6PGiuRLMJOiP9ikjxQAhWy-BpFCXWolN_FF7HO?key=SlNDR1_EiVyJAAvkYCDrSg)
Google Earth Pro is the oldest and original version of Google Earth. It is free of charge and can be installed on a Windows, Mac or Linux computer. It can be downloaded from here: <https://www.google.com/earth/versions/#earth-pro>. Be sure to click the "Download Earth Pro on desktop" button in the middle of the screen. Do not click the blue “Launch Earth” button, this is for the web version.Once Google Earth Pro is installed you will find it in the Windows start menu or the Mac Applications folder. Google Earth Pro is still being maintained and updated.
In Google Earth Pro any placemarks, paths, etc that you add to your My Places are stored locally on your computer, there is no link to your Google account. This means that if you have a new computer you need to transfer the file manually, see [_Move saved locations to a new computer_](https://support.google.com/earth/answer/166438). It’s also a good idea to take regular backups, just right click your top level My Places folder and “Save place as” to a different location on your computer or backup medium.
Google Earth Pro also allows you to get directions, and import GPX, CSV and shape files.
  * [_Help for Google Earth Pro_](https://support.google.com/earth/#topic=7357865) (if you see a banner with a link recommending the developer site, ignore it, that is for the web and mobile versions).
  * [_Google Earth Outreach tutorials_](https://www.google.com/earth/outreach/learn/).
  * [_KML reference_](https://developers.google.com/kml/documentation/kmlreference) for advanced help for creating and editing KML files..


**Google Earth for web**
Google Earth for web is available here [_https://earth.google.com/web/_](https://earth.google.com/web/). 
  * [_Help for Google Earth web and mobile_](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/earth).


Google Earth for web has a home screen listing all the projects you've created or opened.
From the home screen click the "Explore Earth" button top right to access the globe and the imagery.
![](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdUIYnXSGNisQTOyY0q9_182gKqk5mxdUUL6F_iTmgcB5vUMuIcbBNGKBbU-mu_jL0cHzr4X-k1UW0OT8tVR04-Bg_90EMTe45fYZ7c0WiBixyoJ5Q-YuT6v-Ab0mcKr4EYVRgp?key=SlNDR1_EiVyJAAvkYCDrSg)
From the Earth view screen click the globe icon top left, or use the keyboard shortcut ctrl+O to access the home screen with the project list.
![](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcO9gLi4ogz7VRZTGiEtxH0PCb5_EXvDkCPBhjUBmjLD8umUOPRuY5Zw4tq2ENvbiRQziYVh2MgzbVubU2tNk04GMossDYyMLvETSBOQCtvJAiFAq-awdwueI_FgSB_Ps4mJjp8gA?key=SlNDR1_EiVyJAAvkYCDrSg)
To choose whether you want Earth to open to the “Home screen” or “Explore Earth”, click the cog icon top right to open the settings.
Google Earth for web allows you to create and edit projects which are automatically saved to Google Drive.
You can also create, import and export KML and KMZ files. KML, or Keyhole Markup Language, is the file format used to display geographic data in Google Earth Pro. KMZ is a zipped format. KML files can now be imported into a new or existing project. These options are in the File menu or via the + New button on the home screen.
To display more than one project, use the reference project option in the Layers, see [_Understanding Reference Projects_](https://support.google.com/earth/community-guide/311643292).
Any KML file you open or create is stored in your browser's internal storage and can easily disappear if browsing data is cleared. So if you're working with KML files it’s advisable to make frequent back ups. Use the “Export as KML” option in the three dot overflow menu to do this.
There is now a map view with no imagery. To access it click the map thumbnail bottom left. Other layers can also be selected there.
New data layers are behind the layers icon in the top toolbar. See [_Learn about Google Earth plans_](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/earth/earth-plans) for more information.
To change the view, hold down the shift key and the left mouse button, and drag the mouse up/down to tilt, or left/right to rotate.
Google Earth Voyager can be found here: [_https://www.google.com/earth/about/gallery/_](https://www.google.com/earth/about/gallery/). 
You can send feedback using the option in the Help menu.
**Google Earth for Android and iOS**
Google Earth for mobile can be downloaded and installed on Android or iOS devices from the Play Store or App Store.
Google Earth for mobile has a home screen listing all the projects you've created or opened.
From the home screen click the "Explore Earth" button at the bottom of the screen to access the globe and the imagery.
From the Earth view screen click the globe icon bottom left to access the home screen with the project list.
![](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdw-s79cOkgi4Fdb3GVRlLJFri80Zii67rAl-XwAxwyYChTAQSqHGqjWM0-11KzJ1MhYAFKwePLCVh0qd0EJyCaHhnUoewc2mhDwvlUjm6g_aDkT0zs42Z0Phg6lmCV_626dQVxew?key=SlNDR1_EiVyJAAvkYCDrSg)
The menu is accessed by tapping your profile picture or initial. To choose whether you want Earth to open to the “Home screen” or “Explore Earth”: from the Earth view screen, open the menu, select “Settings” and scroll down to the “Display settings” section.
You can create and edit projects with Google Earth for mobile, and they will be automatically saved to Google Drive.
You can also create, import and export KML and KMZ files. KML, or Keyhole Markup Language, is the file format used to display geographic data in Google Earth Pro. KMZ is a zipped format. KML files can now be imported into a new or existing project. These options are accessed via the + New button on the home screen.
To display more than one project, use the reference project option in the Layers, see [_Understanding Reference Projects_](https://support.google.com/earth/community-guide/311643292).
There is now a map view with no imagery. To access it click the map thumbnail top right.
New data layers are behind the layers icon in the bottom toolbar. See [_Learn about Google Earth plans_](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/earth/earth-plans) for more information.
To see the coordinates for a location, long press to drop a pin. Tap Location or Elevation to copy the data to the clipboard for use elsewhere.
To rotate the view use two fingers and turn. 
To tilt the view, tap with two fingers and move up or down. 
Note that the compass only appears when north is not up. Tap the compass to set north up again. Tap the 2d button to reset the tilt.
To access the “I’m feeling lucky” option, tap the search bar, and it will appear below that.
Questions? Feel free to [_ask a new question_](https://support.google.com/earth/thread/new) in the Google Earth help community. Don’t forget to tell us which version you are using!
